targetAudience: PMs and engineers evaluating AI agents
topic: Measuring an agent only by whether the final answer was right
coreInsight: A correct final answer can hide wrong tool calls, wasted steps and risky actions, so evaluate an agent’s trajectory — tools, steps and unapproved actions — not just its output.

hookVariants.text: Your agent passed the eval and still emailed a customer.
Grading agents on the final answer is half an eval.

selectionRationale: Highest total (24/25): a crisp contrast that the card flips prove and the table turns into checks.

script.onScreen: Right answer. Wrong path. / Grade how your agent got there.
script.voiceover: Right answer. Wrong path. Grade how your agent got there.

script.onScreen: THREE RUNS (ILLUSTRATIVE) / All three got the answer right. / FINAL ANSWER Run 1: correct answer → PATH OK Called the right tools · FINAL ANSWER Run 2: correct answer → PATH WASTEFUL Took 14 steps for a 3-step job · FINAL ANSWER Run 3: correct answer → PATH RISKY Emailed a customer by mistake
script.voiceover: Three illustrative runs, all with the right answer. Run one used the right tools. Run two took fourteen steps for a three-step job. Run three emailed a customer by mistake.

script.onScreen: GRADE THE TRAJECTORY / Check the path, not just the end. / CHECK → LOOK FOR → FAIL IF / Tool choice → Right tool, right args → Wrong or made-up tool · Steps taken → Close to expected → Loops or detours · Risky actions → Approved first → Any unapproved write / Log every step, not just the output · Review failed paths, even on passes
script.voiceover: Grade the trajectory: the right tool with the right arguments, a step count close to expected, and no risky action without approval. Log every step, and review bad paths even when the answer passed.

caption:
An agent can reach the right answer the wrong way, and a final-answer eval will score it a pass.

What a final-answer check misses:
→ the wrong tool, or made-up arguments, that happened to work
→ fourteen steps for a three-step job (cost and latency)
→ an action nobody approved, like sending an email

Grade the trajectory too:
→ tool choice and arguments
→ step count against what you expect
→ any write or external action without approval = fail

(The three runs in the reel are illustrative examples.)

Save this for your agent eval plan.
